tools_helpful.evidence: session-log: 'Rewrote Windows.UI.Xaml -> Microsoft.UI.Xaml in 5 of 11 .cs/.xaml files' — bulk namespace rewrite worked and scaffolded the project.

Agent correctly added WinRT.Interop.InitializeWithWindow.Initialize(picker, hwnd) for FileOpenPicker (commit note: 'Fix FileOpenPicker: add InitializeWithWindow for WinUI 3 desktop'), matching the dedicated pickers pattern at MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md:272-279.

tool_limitations.limitation: Its mass namespace rewrite only handles 'Windows.UI.Xaml' -> 'Microsoft.UI.Xaml'. Non-Xaml WinRT UI namespaces that ALSO moved to the Microsoft.UI root (Windows.UI.Colors, Windows.UI.ColorHelper) are left untouched, so they fail to compile after bootstrap and the agent must find/fix them by hand.
tool_limitations.suggested_tweak: Extend the rewrite to also map 'Windows.UI.Colors' -> 'Microsoft.UI.Colors' and 'Windows.UI.ColorHelper' -> 'Microsoft.UI.ColorHelper' (word-boundary matched so the 'Windows.UI.Color' struct is NOT touched).

failed_apis.why_tried: UWP source set SolidColorBrush(Windows.UI.Colors.Green/Red) for status border coloring; agent first left 'Windows.UI.Colors' (does not exist in WinAppSDK) then rewrote to bare 'Colors' with no 'using Microsoft.UI;'.
failed_apis.root_cause: 'Colors' and 'ColorHelper' static classes moved from Windows.UI to the Microsoft.UI namespace (NOT Microsoft.UI.Xaml), and the bootstrap script's Windows.UI.Xaml rewrite does not cover them.
failed_apis.fix: Fully qualify as Microsoft.UI.Colors.Green / Microsoft.UI.Colors.Red (or add 'using Microsoft.UI;'). Confirmed in session-log turn rewriting bare Colors -> Microsoft.UI.Colors.

doc_errors.wrong: Header states 'All Windows.UI.Xaml.* namespaces move to Microsoft.UI.Xaml.*' but the same table lists non-Xaml rows (Windows.UI.Colors, Windows.UI.Text, Windows.UI.Core). It never states that the bootstrap auto-rewrite ONLY covers the Windows.UI.Xaml rows, so a reader assumes Colors is handled too.
doc_errors.correct: Split/annotate the table to mark which rows the bootstrap auto-rewrites vs. which are manual, and note Colors/ColorHelper land in Microsoft.UI (not Microsoft.UI.Xaml) while the Windows.UI.Color struct stays put.

special_apis.special_handling: Move to Microsoft.UI (root), unlike everything else under Windows.UI.Xaml which moves to Microsoft.UI.Xaml. The value struct Windows.UI.Color does NOT move.
Require WinRT.Interop.InitializeWithWindow.Initialize(picker, hwnd) in desktop WinUI 3 — already covered well by the skill; agent applied it correctly.

errors_encountered.error: CS0103: The name 'Colors' does not exist in the current context (MainPage.xaml.cs:125,128)
errors_encountered.root_cause: Windows.UI.Colors -> bare Colors without importing Microsoft.UI; static class moved to Microsoft.UI, not covered by the bootstrap Windows.UI.Xaml rewrite.

errors_encountered.error: CS8803 'Top-level statements must precede namespace/type declarations' + CS1022 'end-of-file expected' + repeated CS0106 'modifier not valid for this item' across Scenario1_LaunchFile.xaml.cs / Scenario2_LaunchUri.xaml.cs
errors_encountered.root_cause: A stray/extra closing brace introduced while editing the large partial-class code-behind prematurely closed the class+namespace, so subsequent methods parsed as top-level statements. Pure editing slip, recovered within a few build iterations (18 successful builds overall).
errors_encountered.fix: Re-balanced braces so all members stay inside the class body.

dev_agent_struggles.symptom: CS0103 'Colors' does not exist; two rewrite attempts (Windows.UI.Colors -> bare Colors -> Microsoft.UI.Colors) before it compiled.
dev_agent_struggles.root_cause: Bootstrap script only rewrites Windows.UI.Xaml; Colors/ColorHelper moved to Microsoft.UI and were left broken, and the mapping table under-emphasizes this.
dev_agent_struggles.preventable_by: Extend Initialize-UwpMigration.ps1 to also rewrite Windows.UI.Colors/ColorHelper -> Microsoft.UI.* and sharpen the namespace-mapping doc to flag auto vs. manual rows.

dev_agent_struggles.symptom: CS8803/CS1022/CS0106 cluster from an unbalanced brace after an in-place edit of the code-behind.
dev_agent_struggles.root_cause: Editing typo (extra closing brace) in a large partial class — not a UWP knowledge gap.
dev_agent_struggles.preventable_by: Generic editing care / build-after-edit; no skill content would prevent a stray-brace typo. (dev-agent-slip)
